citation: Revheim I, Ballance S, Standal AF et al. (2024). The acute effect of a β-glucan-enriched oat bread on gastric emptying, GLP-1 response, and postprandial glycaemia and insulinemia: a randomised crossover trial in healthy adults. Nutrition & Metabolism 21:13.
protocol: Two breads, randomised crossover, 25 g available carbohydrate each: beta-glucan-enriched oat bread (94.1 g; 5.5 g fibre, 3.6 g beta-glucan, 2.9 g fat, 7.6 g protein) vs whole-wheat bread (60.1 g; 2.4 g fibre, 3.1 g fat, 4.1 g protein). Blood at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min.
population: n=22 healthy adults (8 men, 14 women), age 24.6 ± 3.1 y, BMI 23.1 ± 2.7 kg/m2 (Table 2).

reports.where: Results text: iAUC 0-2 h, Cmax and Tmax per bread (mean ± SD)
Results text: iAUC, Cmax, Tmax per bread

note: Paired-meal contrast, fibre: whole-wheat bread vs beta-glucan-enriched oat bread at matched available carbohydrate. Viscous-fibre contrast with gastric emptying measured alongside.
